sanskrit: tataḥ sa madhyaṃ gatam aṃśumantaṃ jyotsnāvitānaṃ mahad udvamantam dadarśa dhīmān divi bhānumantaṃ goṣṭhe vṛṣaṃ mattam iva bhramantam
english: Then that wise one beheld in the sky the Moon, who had reached the zenith, pouring out a great flood of moonlight, blazing with radiance, roaming like a rutting bull in a cattle-pen.

sanskrit: lokasya pāpāni vināśayantaṃ mahodadhiṃ cāpi samedhayantam bhūtāni sarvāṇi virājayantaṃ dadarśa śītāṃśum athābhiyāntam
english: He beheld the cool-rayed Moon advancing — destroying the sins of the world, swelling the great ocean, and illuminating all living beings.

sanskrit: yā bhāti lakṣmīr bhuvi mandarasthā tathā pradoṣeṣu ca sāgarasthā tathaiva toyeṣu ca puṣkarasthā rarāja sā cāruniśākarasthā
english: The beauty that shines on earth when set upon Mandara, and at nightfall when resting upon the ocean, and likewise when dwelling in lotus-pools — that same splendour now blazed, abiding in the lovely Moon.

sanskrit: haṃso yathā rājatapañjurasthaḥ siṃho yathā mandarakandarasthaḥ vīro yathā garvitakuñjarasthaś candro 'pi babhrāja tathāmbarasthaḥ
english: As a swan resting in a silver cage, as a lion couched in a cave of Mandara, as a hero mounted on a proud elephant — so too the Moon blazed, stationed in the sky.

sanskrit: sthitaḥ kakudmān iva tīkṣṇaśṛṅgo mahācalaḥ śveta ivoccaśṛṅgaḥ hastīva jāmbūnadabaddhaśṛṅgo vibhāti candraḥ paripūrṇaśṛṅgaḥ
english: Like a great mountain with a sharp summit, like a white peak rising high, like an elephant with its tusks bound in gold — so the Moon shone with its disc perfectly full.

sanskrit: prakāśacandrodayanaṣṭadoṣaḥ pravṛddharakṣaḥ piśitāśadoṣaḥ rāmābhirāmeritacittadoṣaḥ svargaprakāśo bhagavān pradoṣaḥ
english: The blessed nightfall had its faults dispelled by the bright rising of the Moon; the fault of the flesh-eating Rākṣasas grown mighty; the fault of minds stirred by longing for lovely Rāma — yet it shone like heaven.

sanskrit: tantrī svanāḥ karṇasukhāḥ pravṛttāḥ svapanti nāryaḥ patibhiḥ suvṛttāḥ naktaṃcarāś cāpi tathā pravṛttā vihartum atyadbhutaraudravṛttāḥ
english: Sweet sounds of lutes and strings, pleasing to the ear, arose; women of good conduct slept beside their husbands; and the night-wanderers too stirred forth to sport — those of most wondrous and dread disposition.

sanskrit: mattapramattāni samākulāni rathāśvabhadrāsanasaṃkulāni vīraśriyā cāpi samākulāni dadarśa dhīmān sa kapiḥ kulāni
english: That wise monkey beheld households in tumult with the intoxicated and the heedless, filled with chariots, horses, and fine seats, and thronged with the glory of heroes.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ cādhikam ākṣipanti bhujāṃś ca pīnān adhivikṣipanti mattapralāpān adhivikṣipanti mattāni cānyonyam adhikṣipanti
english: They hurled boastful taunts at one another, flinging their stout arms about, uttering the babbling speech of the intoxicated, casting challenges at each other in their drunkenness.

sanskrit: rakṣāṃsi vakṣāṃsi ca vikṣipanti gātrāṇi kāntāsu ca vikṣipanti dadarśa kāntāś ca samālapanti tathāparās tatra punaḥ svapanti
english: Rākṣasas throwing out their broad chests, casting their limbs upon their beloved women — he saw some conversing with their sweethearts, and others there sleeping.

sanskrit: mahāgajaiś cāpi tathā nadadbhiḥ sūpūjitaiś cāpi tathā susadbhiḥ rarāja vīraiś ca viniḥśvasadbhir hrado bhujaṅgair iva niḥśvasadbhiḥ
english: It resounded with great elephants trumpeting, with well-worshipped and excellent horses, with heroes heaving sighs — gleaming like a lake breathing with serpents.

sanskrit: buddhipradhānān rucirābhidhānān saṃśraddadhānāñ jagataḥ pradhānān nānāvidhānān rucirābhidhānān dadarśa tasyāṃ puri yātudhānān
english: In that city he saw Yātudhānas — the demon-sorcerers — foremost in intellect, bearing lovely names, revered and regarded as chiefs of the world, of many varieties and with pleasing appellations.

sanskrit: nananda dṛṣṭvā sa ca tān surūpān nānāguṇān ātmaguṇānurūpān vidyotamānān sa ca tān surūpān dadarśa kāṃś cic ca punar virūpān
english: He rejoiced to see those of fair form, endowed with varied qualities befitting their own natures, blazing with splendour — those of beautiful form he saw; and then again some others of hideous form.

sanskrit: tato varārhāḥ suviśuddhabhāvās teṣāṃ striyas tatra mahānubhāvāḥ priyeṣu pāneṣu ca saktabhāvā dadarśa tārā iva suprabhāvāḥ
english: Then he saw the wives of those Rākṣasas — women worthy of the best, with hearts utterly pure, of great majesty, devoted in spirit to their beloved drinks, shining like stars of brilliant radiance.

sanskrit: śriyā jvalantīs trapayopagūḍhā niśīthakāle ramaṇopagūḍhāḥ dadarśa kāś cit pramadopagūḍhā yathā vihaṃgāḥ kusumopagūḍāḥ
english: Blazing with beauty, veiled by modesty, in the midnight hour clasped by their lovers — he saw some women embraced by their beloved mates, like birds nestled amid blossoms.

sanskrit: anyāḥ punar harmyatalopaviṣṭās tatra priyāṅkeṣu sukhopaviṣṭāḥ bhartuḥ priyā dharmaparā niviṣṭā dadarśa dhīmān manadābhiviṣṭāḥ
english: Others again were seated on the floors of their mansions, comfortably settled in the laps of their beloved husbands — devoted to virtue, dear to their lords, well-settled in their place — and that wise one saw them possessed of a dignity that confers honour.

sanskrit: aprāvṛtāḥ kāñcanarājivarṇāḥ kāś cit parārdhyās tapanīyavarṇāḥ punaś ca kāś cic chaśalakṣmavarṇāḥ kāntaprahīṇā rucirāṅgavarṇāḥ
english: Some were unclothed, of golden-streak complexion; some were most precious ones of burnished-gold hue; others again were of lunar-spot colouring; and some, deserted by their lovers, were of lovely limb-colour.

sanskrit: tataḥ priyān prāpya mano'bhirāmān suprītiyuktāḥ prasamīkṣya rāmāḥ gṛheṣu hṛṣṭāḥ paramābhirāmā haripravīraḥ sa dadarśa rāmāḥ
english: Then, having obtained their beloved ones who delight the mind, filled with deep joy, looking upon those Rāmas — the lord of monkeys beheld those women, joyful in their homes and supremely beautiful.

sanskrit: candraprakāśāś ca hi vaktramālā vakrākṣipakṣmāś ca sunetramālāḥ vibhūṣaṇānāṃ ca dadarśa mālāḥ śatahradānām iva cārumālāḥ
english: He saw garlands of faces bright as moonlight, garlands of lovely eyes with curving lashes, garlands of ornaments — like the fair garland of the hundred-flash lightning.

sanskrit: na tv eva sītāṃ paramābhijātāṃ pathi sthite rājakule prajātām latāṃ praphullām iva sādhujātāṃ dadarśa tanvīṃ manasābhijātām
english: But Sītā, of the highest birth, born into the royal line that walks the righteous path, slender as a blossoming vine of noble growth — born of the mind itself — he did not find her.

sanskrit: sanātane vartmani saṃniviṣṭāṃ rāmekṣaṇīṃ tāṃ madanābhiviṣṭām bhartur manaḥ śrīmad anupraviṣṭāṃ strībhyo varābhyaś ca sadā viśiṣṭām
english: Her who is established in the eternal path, that one worthy to be seen by Rāma, seized by longing, who has entered the glorious mind of her husband — ever distinguished above all excellent women — he did not see.

sanskrit: uṣṇārditāṃ sānusṛtāsrakaṇṭhīṃ purā varārhottamaniṣkakaṇṭhīm sujātapakṣmām abhiraktakaṇṭhīṃ vane pravṛttām iva nīlakaṇṭhīm
english: Afflicted by heat, her throat flowing with streaming tears, her throat once adorned with the finest and most precious jewelled pendants, with well-formed lashes, her throat flushed — wandering in the forest like a blue-throated bird — he did not see her.

sanskrit: avyaktalekhām iva candralekhāṃ pāṃsupradigdhām iva hemalekhām kṣataprarūḍhām iva bāṇalekhāṃ vāyuprabhinnām iva meghalekhām
english: Like the crescent of the moon with its mark obscured; like a line of gold smeared with dust; like the track of an arrow-wound grown over again; like a streak of cloud rent asunder by the wind.

sanskrit: sītām apaśyan manujeśvarasya rāmasya patnīṃ vadatāṃ varasya babhūva duḥkhābhihataś cirasya plavaṃgamo manda ivācirasya
english: Not finding Sītā — wife of Rāma, lord of men, best among the eloquent — the monkey became struck with grief, growing slow and sluggish after long exertion, like a fire robbed of its vigour.

sanskrit: sa nikāmaṃ vināmeṣu vicaran kāmarūpadhṛk vicacāra kapir laṅkāṃ lāghavena samanvitaḥ
english: Roaming at will among the bending trees, the monkey, assuming whatever form he desired, explored Laṅkā with swiftness and ease.

sanskrit: āsasādātha lakṣmīvān rākṣasendraniveśanam prākāreṇārkavarṇena bhāsvareṇābhisaṃvṛtam
english: Then that glorious one came upon the palace of the lord of Rākṣasas, entirely enclosed by a wall of sun-like colour and radiant splendour.

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ rākṣasair bhīmaiḥ siṃhair iva mahad vanam samīkṣamāṇo bhavanaṃ cakāśe kapikuñjaraḥ
english: Guarded by terrible Rākṣasas as a great forest is guarded by lions — surveying that mansion, the elephant among monkeys shone forth with purpose.

sanskrit: rūpyakopahitaiś citrais toraṇair hemabhūṣitaiḥ vicitrābhiś ca kakṣyābhir dvāraiś ca rucirair vṛtam
english: It was adorned with variegated gateways fitted with silver finials and decorated with gold, surrounded by elaborate courtyards and beautiful doors.

sanskrit: gajāsthitair mahāmātraiḥ śūraiś ca vigataśramaiḥ upasthitam asaṃhāryair hayaiḥ syandanayāyibhiḥ
english: It was attended by great elephant-drivers mounted on their elephants, by tireless heroes, by irresistible horses and chariot-riders.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghratanutrāṇair dāntakāñcanarājataiḥ ghoṣavadbhir vicitraiś ca sadā vicaritaṃ rathaiḥ
english: It was constantly traversed by chariots with armour made of lion and tiger hide, wrought of ivory, gold, and silver, resonant with noise and richly adorned.

sanskrit: bahuratnasamākīrṇaṃ parārdhyāsanabhājanam mahārathasamāvāsaṃ mahārathamahāsanam
english: It was strewn with many precious gems, filled with vessels of the most valuable seats, the dwelling-place of great warriors, furnished with great thrones for great car-warriors.

sanskrit: dṛśyaiś ca paramodārais tais taiś ca mṛgapakṣibhiḥ vividhair bahusāhasraiḥ paripūrṇaṃ samantataḥ
english: It was filled on all sides with various most excellent spectacles, and with various beasts and birds in their thousands upon thousands.

sanskrit: vinītair antapālaiś ca rakṣobhiś ca surakṣitam mukhyābhiś ca varastrībhiḥ paripūrṇaṃ samantataḥ
english: It was well-guarded by well-trained gate-keepers and Rākṣasa guards, and filled everywhere with foremost women of the finest quality.

sanskrit: muditapramadā ratnaṃ rākṣasendraniveśanam varābharaṇanirhrādaiḥ samudrasvananiḥsvanam
english: That jewel of a palace of the lord of Rākṣasas, filled with joyful women, resounded with the tinkling of exquisite ornaments like the roar of the ocean.

sanskrit: tad rājaguṇasaṃpannaṃ mukhyaiś ca varacandanaiḥ bherīmṛdaṅgābhirutaṃ śaṅkhaghoṣavināditam
english: That palace, endowed with every royal excellence, perfumed with the finest sandalwood, resounded with the beat of kettledrums and mṛdaṅgas, and rang with the blast of conch-shells.

sanskrit: nityārcitaṃ parvahutaṃ pūjitaṃ rākṣasaiḥ sadā samudram iva gambhīraṃ samudram iva niḥsvanam
english: Perpetually worshipped, offered oblations at every festival, constantly honoured by the Rākṣasas — deep as the ocean, and resonant as the ocean.

sanskrit: mahātmāno mahad veśma mahāratnaparicchadam mahājanasamākīrṇaṃ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
english: That great monkey of mighty soul beheld the vast dwelling, furnished with most precious appurtenances, thronged with great multitudes of people.

sanskrit: virājamānaṃ vapuṣā gajāśvarathasaṃkulam laṅkābharaṇam ity eva so 'manyata mahākapiḥ
english: Blazing with splendour in its form, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots — that great monkey reckoned it to be the very ornament of Laṅkā itself.

sanskrit: gṛhād gṛhaṃ rākṣasānām udyānāni ca vānaraḥ vīkṣamāṇo hy asaṃtrastaḥ prāsādāṃś ca cacāra saḥ
english: Moving from house to house among the Rākṣasas, surveying the gardens and the palace-towers without any fear, that monkey roamed about.

sanskrit: avaplutya mahāvegaḥ prahastasya niveśanam tato 'nyat pupluve veśma mahāpārśvasya vīryavān
english: Leaping with great speed into the mansion of Prahasta, that mighty one then bounded to another dwelling — the mansion of Mahāpārśva.

sanskrit: atha meghapratīkāśaṃ kumbhakarṇaniveśanam vibhīṣaṇasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ
english: Then that great monkey leaped into the dwelling of Kumbhakarṇa, resembling a thundercloud, and likewise into that of Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: mahodarasya ca tathā virūpākṣasya caiva hi vidyujjihvasya bhavanaṃ vidyunmāles tathaiva ca vajradaṃṣṭrasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ
english: And likewise into the mansion of Mahodara, and of Virūpākṣa, into the dwelling of Vidyujjihvā, and likewise that of Vidyunmālin, and the dwelling of Vajradaṃṣṭra — so that great monkey leaped.

sanskrit: śukasya ca mahāvegaḥ sāraṇasya ca dhīmataḥ tathā cendrajitos veśma jagāma hariyūthapaḥ
english: With great speed, the leader of the monkey-horde went to the mansion of Śuka, and of the wise Sāraṇa, and likewise to the dwelling of Indrajit.

sanskrit: jambumāleḥ sumāleś ca jagāma hariyūthapaḥ raśmiketoś ca bhavanaṃ sūryaśatros tathaiva ca
english: The leader of the monkey-horde went to the mansions of Jambumālin and Sumālin, and likewise to the dwelling of Raśmiketu and Sūryaśatru.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣasya ca saṃpāter bhavanaṃ mārutātmajaḥ vidyudrūpasya bhīmasya ghanasya vighanasya ca
english: The son of the Wind visited the mansion of Dhūmrākṣa and Saṃpātin, of the dreadful Vidyudrūpa, of Ghana and of Vighana.

sanskrit: śukanābhasya vakrasya śaṭhasya vikaṭasya ca hrasvakarṇasya daṃṣṭrasya romaśasya ca rakṣasaḥ
english: He visited the mansions of Śukanābha, of Vakra, of Śaṭha and Vikaṭa, of Hrasvakarṇa, of Daṃṣṭra, and of the Rākṣasa Romaśa.

sanskrit: yuddhonmattasya mattasya dhvajagrīvasya nādinaḥ vidyujjihvendrajihvānāṃ tathā hastimukhasya ca
english: He visited those of Yuddhonmatta, of Matta, of Dhvajagrīva, of Nādin, of Vidyujjihvā and Indrajihva, and likewise of Hastimukha.

sanskrit: karālasya piśācasya śoṇitākṣasya caiva hi kramamāṇaḥ krameṇaiva hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: And of Karāla, of Piśāca, and of Śoṇitākṣa — advancing step by step in due order, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, moved on.

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu mahārheṣu bhavaneṣu mahāyaśāḥ teṣām ṛddhimatām ṛddhiṃ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
english: In each of those most magnificent mansions, that great monkey of great glory beheld the opulence of those opulent ones.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ samatikramya bhavanāni samantataḥ āsasādātha lakṣmīvān rākṣasendraniveśanam
english: Having passed through all the mansions on every side, that glorious one then arrived at the palace of the lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasyopaśāyinyo dadarśa harisattamaḥ vicaran hariśārdūlo rākṣasīr vikṛtekṣaṇāḥ śūlamudgarahastāś ca śakto tomaradhāriṇīḥ
english: That foremost of monkeys, that tiger among monkeys, roaming about, beheld the female Rākṣasas who lay in attendance upon Rāvaṇa — those of distorted eyes, bearing tridents and cudgels in their hands, armed with śakti-spears and bearing tomaras.

sanskrit: dadarśa vividhān gulmāṃs tasya rakṣaḥpater gṛhe
english: He beheld the various guard-posts in the dwelling of that lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: raktāñ śvetān sitāṃś caiva harīṃś caiva mahājavān kulīnān rūpasaṃpannān gajān paragajārujān
english: Red ones, white ones, and pale ones — and tawny ones of great speed, of noble lineage, endowed with fine form — elephants that break the elephants of enemies.

sanskrit: niṣṭhitān gajaśikhāyām airāvatasamān yudhi nihantṝn parasainyānāṃ gṛhe tasmin dadarśa saḥ
english: He saw in that dwelling those trained in the peak of elephant-craft, the equals of Airāvata in battle, the slayers of enemy armies.

sanskrit: kṣarataś ca yathā meghān sravataś ca yathā girīn meghastanitanirghoṣān durdharṣān samare paraiḥ
english: Dripping like rain-clouds, oozing like mountains weeping — producing a roar like the thunder of clouds, unconquerable by enemies in battle.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ vāhinīs tatra jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtāḥ hemajālair avicchinnās taruṇādityasaṃnibhāḥ
english: A thousand companies of troops were there, adorned with gold of the Jambū river, unbroken by nets of gold, resembling the young sun.

sanskrit: dadarśa rākṣasendrasya rāvaṇasya niveśane śibikā vividhākārāḥ sa kapir mārutātmajaḥ
english: That monkey, the son of the Wind, beheld in the palace of Rāvaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas, palanquins of various shapes and forms.

sanskrit: latāgṛhāṇi citrāṇi citraśālāgṛhāṇi ca krīḍāgṛhāṇi cānyāni dāruparvatakān api
english: Lovely bower-houses of creepers, and painted hall-chambers, and other pleasure-houses, and also wooden model mountains.

sanskrit: kāmasya gṛhakaṃ ramyaṃ divāgṛhakam eva ca dadarśa rākṣasendrasya rāvaṇasya niveśane
english: The charming house of pleasures, and also the daytime-chamber — these he beheld in the palace of Rāvaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa mandaratalaprakhyaṃ mayūrasthānasaṃkulam dhvajayaṣṭibhir ākīrṇaṃ dadarśa bhavanottamam
english: He beheld that most excellent of mansions — resembling the surface of Mount Mandara, crowded with peacock-grounds, and thickly planted with flag-poles.

sanskrit: anantaratnanicayaṃ nidhijālaṃ samantataḥ dhīraniṣṭhitakarmāntaṃ gṛhaṃ bhūtapater iva
english: With a mass of infinite gems, a treasury on every side, with all work-tasks executed steadily and surely — like the palace of the lord of all beings.

sanskrit: arcirbhiś cāpi ratnānāṃ tejasā rāvaṇasya ca virarājātha tad veśma raśmimān iva raśmibhiḥ
english: And with the flames of gemstones and the splendour of Rāvaṇa himself — that mansion then blazed forth like the sun radiating its rays.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayāny eva śayanāny āsanāni ca bhājanāni ca śubhrāṇi dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ
english: Couches and seats made entirely of Jāmbūnada gold, and bright, gleaming vessels — these the leader of the monkey-host beheld.

sanskrit: madhvāsavakṛtakledaṃ maṇibhājanasaṃkulam manoramam asaṃbādhaṃ kuberabhavanaṃ yathā
english: Moist with the residue of honey-wine, crowded with jewelled vessels, delightful and unencumbered — like the palace of Kubera himself.

sanskrit: nūpurāṇāṃ ca ghoṣeṇa kāñcīnāṃ ninadena ca mṛdaṅgatalaghoṣaiś ca ghoṣavadbhir vināditam
english: It resounded with the jingling of anklets, with the tinkling of golden girdles, and rang out loudly with the sound of mṛdaṅga-drums and clapping hands.

sanskrit: prāsādasaṃghātayutaṃ strīratnaśatasaṃkulam suvyūḍhakakṣyaṃ hanumān praviveśa mahāgṛham
english: Provided with an assemblage of palace-towers, thronged with hundreds of jewel-like women, with its courtyards well-arranged — Hanūmān entered that great mansion.

sanskrit: sa veśmajālaṃ balavān dadarśa vyāsaktavaidūryasuvarṇajālam yathā mahat prāvṛṣi meghajālaṃ vidyutpinaddhaṃ savihaṃgajālam
english: That mighty one beheld a network of dwelling-chambers, interlaced with a lattice of vaidūrya gems and gold — like a great canopy of clouds in the rainy season, bound together by lightning and interwoven with flights of birds.

sanskrit: niveśanānāṃ vividhāś ca śālāḥ pradhānaśaṅkhāyudhacāpaśālāḥ manoharāś cāpi punar viśālā dadarśa veśmādriṣu candraśālāḥ
english: Various halls of the palatial residences — halls foremost with conches, weapons, and bows — and also charming and spacious moonlit terraces on the palace-mountains: these he beheld.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇi nānāvasurājitāni devāsuraiś cāpi supūjitāni sarvaiś ca doṣaiḥ parivarjitāni kapir dadarśa svabalārjitāni
english: Mansions glorified by many kinds of jewels, well-honoured even by gods and asuras, free from all faults — the monkey beheld those acquired by his own prowess.

sanskrit: tāni prayatnābhisamāhitāni mayena sākṣād iva nirmitāni mahītale sarvaguṇottarāṇi dadarśa laṅkādhipater gṛhāṇi
english: Those mansions brought together with great care, built as if by Maya himself in person, surpassing all in every excellence on the face of the earth — he beheld those homes of the lord of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: tato dadarśocchritamegharūpaṃ manoharaṃ kāñcanacārurūpam rakṣo'dhipasyātmabalānurūpaṃ gṛhottamaṃ hy apratirūparūpam
english: Then he beheld the most excellent of mansions — towering in the form of a great cloud, charming and beautiful with golden appearance, commensurate with the personal might of the lord of Rākṣasas, matchless in form and without equal.

sanskrit: mahītale svargam iva prakīrṇaṃ śriyā jvalantaṃ bahuratnakīrṇam nānātarūṇāṃ kusumāvakīrṇaṃ girer ivāgraṃ rajasāvakīrṇam
english: Like heaven spread out upon the earth, blazing with glory, strewn with many gems, strewn with blossoms of manifold trees — like the summit of a mountain sprinkled with pollen.

sanskrit: nārīpravekair iva dīpyamānaṃ taḍidbhir ambhodavad arcyamānam haṃsapravekair iva vāhyamānaṃ śriyā yutaṃ khe sukṛtāṃ vimānam
english: Blazing as if with the finest of women; worshipped like a rain-cloud by lightning-flashes; carried as if by the finest of swans — that heavenly vimāna-palace shone in the sky, endowed with glory, the dwelling of those who have performed great merit.

sanskrit: yathā nagāgraṃ bahudhātucitraṃ yathā nabhaś ca grahacandracitram dadarśa yuktīkṛtameghacitraṃ vimānaratnaṃ bahuratnacitram
english: As the peak of a mountain is variegated with many minerals, as the sky is variegated with planets and the moon — he beheld that jewel of a vimāna, variegated with artfully fashioned clouds, variegated with many precious stones.

sanskrit: mahī kṛtā parvatarājipūrṇā śailāḥ kṛtā vṛkṣavitānapūrṇāḥ vṛkṣāḥ kṛtā puṣpavitānapūrṇāḥ puṣpaṃ kṛtaṃ kesarapatrapūrṇam
english: The earth was fashioned full of ranges of mountains; the mountains were fashioned full of spreading canopies of trees; the trees were fashioned full of spreading canopies of flowers; the flowers were fashioned full of filaments and petals.

sanskrit: kṛtāni veśmāni ca pāṇḍurāṇi tathā supuṣpā api puṣkariṇyaḥ punaś ca padmāni sakesarāṇi dhanyāni citrāṇi tathā vanāni
english: And white mansions were fashioned, and lotus-pools in full bloom; and again lotuses with their stamens, auspicious and variegated, and likewise wonderful forests.

sanskrit: puṣpāhvayaṃ nāma virājamānaṃ ratnaprabhābhiś ca vivardhamānam veśmottamānām api coccamānaṃ mahākapis tatra mahāvimānam
english: Named Puṣpāhvaya — the Flower-named — blazing splendidly, growing ever greater with the radiance of precious gems, rising even above the most excellent of mansions — that great vimāna the great monkey beheld there.

sanskrit: kṛtāś ca vaidūryamayā vihaṃgā rūpyapravālaiś ca tathā vihaṃgāḥ citrāś ca nānāvasubhir bhujaṃgā jātyānurūpās turagāḥ śubhāṅgāḥ
english: Birds were fashioned of vaidūrya, and likewise birds of silver and coral; serpents were variegated with many kinds of gems; and horses of fine breeds with beautiful limbs were fashioned.

sanskrit: pravālajāmbūnadapuṣpapakṣāḥ salīlam āvarjitajihmapakṣāḥ kāmasya sākṣād iva bhānti pakṣāḥ kṛtā vihaṃgāḥ sumukhāḥ supakṣāḥ
english: With wings of coral, Jāmbūnada gold, and flowers; with bent, curving wings gracefully inclined — their wings shine as if Kāma himself were manifest; birds were fashioned with beautiful faces and lovely wings.

sanskrit: niyujyamānāś ca gajāḥ suhastāḥ sakesarāś cotpalapatrahastāḥ babhūva devī ca kṛtā suhastā lakṣmīs tathā padmini padmahastā
english: And elephants being yoked, with graceful trunks, bearing lotus-leaves as their trunks — and also the goddess Lakṣmī was fashioned with lovely hands, holding a lotus in the lotus-pool.

sanskrit: itīva tad gṛham abhigamya śobhanaṃ savismayo nagam iva cāruśobhanam punaś ca tat paramasugandhi sundaraṃ himātyaye nagam iva cārukandaram
english: Having approached that beautiful mansion — full of wonder, like a lovely, beautiful mountain — and again that supremely fragrant, lovely one — like a mountain with a beautiful cave at the end of the snowy season.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tāṃ kapir abhipatya pūjitāṃ caran purīṃ daśamukhabāhupālitām adṛśya tāṃ janakasutāṃ supūjitāṃ suduḥkhitāṃ patiguṇaveganirjitām
english: Then that monkey, having traversed that revered city guarded by the arms of the ten-faced Rāvaṇa, not finding that daughter of Janaka — so greatly honoured, so deeply afflicted, overwhelmed by the power of her husband's virtues.

sanskrit: tatas tadā bahuvidhabhāvitātmanaḥ kṛtātmano janakasutāṃ suvartmanaḥ apaśyato 'bhavad atiduḥkhitaṃ manaḥ sucakṣuṣaḥ pravicarato mahātmanaḥ
english: Then at that time, the mind of that great-souled one — whose spirit had been cultivated in many ways, whose self was disciplined, who walked the right path, who roamed with clear vision — became exceedingly grieved at not finding the daughter of Janaka.
